new_public_evidence.source: Hoeffding (1963), Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables; Serfling (1980), U-Statistics chapter
new_public_evidence.result: For a bounded order-m U-statistic, Hoeffding's exponential inequality has effective block count floor(n/m), not the combinatorial number of kernel evaluations. For an indicator order-2 U-CDF this gives pointwise tails with K=floor(n/2). Serfling reproduces the same explicit result and proof via disjoint blocks.

new_public_evidence.source: Clémençon, Lugosi & Vayatis (2008), Ranking and Empirical Minimization of U-statistics
new_public_evidence.result: Their first-order U-process symmetrization reduces the complete order-2 U-process to a Rademacher process over floor(n/2) independent disjoint pairs. This reinforces that complete all-pairs evaluation does not generically provide C(n,2) independent calibration information.

new_public_evidence.source: Vovk & Wang (2021), E-values: Calibration, Combination, and Applications
new_public_evidence.result: A decreasing p-to-e calibrator maps any super-uniform p-variable to an e-variable; the standard family f_kappa(p)=kappa p^(kappa-1), 0<kappa<1, is admissible. Conditional e-value increments can therefore be multiplied into a test e-process when each new p-value is conditionally super-uniform.

derived_results.claim: The all-pairs squared-difference U-empirical CDF cannot be assigned a distribution-free DKW width as if it had C(n,2) independent observations. Generic bounded-U concentration has only K=floor(n/2) in the exponent, and first-order U-process symmetrization likewise uses floor(n/2) disjoint pairs.
derived_results.scope: This rules out the naive effective-sample-size argument and shows that generic distribution-free U-process machinery does not obviously beat the r80 disjoint-pair DKW bottleneck. It does not prove that no sharper inequality exists for the special Gaussian pair-difference kernel.

derived_results.claim: For Gaussian monitoring, the pair-difference U-CDF can be avoided entirely. Estimate an exact chi-square confidence interval [sigma_L,sigma_U] for the unknown baseline standard deviation from all n reference observations. For each disjoint future pair define D=(Y_1-Y_2)/sqrt(2). On the confidence event, p_up=2(1-Phi(|D|/sigma_U)) is super-uniform under the no-change null, and p_down=2Phi(|D|/sigma_L)-1 is also super-uniform. Applying f_kappa(p)=kappa p^(kappa-1) and multiplying sequentially gives two anytime-valid conditional e-processes for variance increase/decrease without estimating a pair-difference ECDF.
derived_results.proof: On the confidence event sigma<=sigma_U, |D|/sigma_U is stochastically no larger than |N(0,1)|, hence the upper-tail p-value is stochastically no smaller than Uniform(0,1). Similarly sigma>=sigma_L makes |D|/sigma_L stochastically no smaller than |N(0,1)|, so its folded-normal lower-tail CDF is super-uniform. Disjoint future pairs are independent conditional on the frozen reference; p-to-e calibration then gives conditional e-value increments.

derived_results.claim: Combining the raw-value conditional CTM with the two variance-CI e-processes gives a parameter-free-in-operation detector portfolio covering every Gaussian alternative with D_KL(Q||P)>=1, while keeping a single global anytime false-alarm budget.

details.branch_logic: If raw PIT-mean signal >=0.163, the raw x conditional-CTM has positive certified effective signal. If it is <0.163, the r80 analytic KL argument forces variance ratio r<0.065 or r>3.4, which is handled by the variance-decrease/increase e-process respectively.

derived_results.scope: Gaussian iid baseline and fixed iid post-change alternative; raw score identity is fixed and requires no fitted centering/scaling; variance channel uses Gaussian chi-square reference inference and disjoint future pairs.

derived_results.claim: At n=684 and variance-CI failure delta=0.01, the central chi-square reference event implies sigma_U/sigma<=1.14972 and sigma_L/sigma>=0.86978. At the conservative branch boundaries r=3.4 and r=0.065, the variance p-values still have strong alternative log signal.
derived_results.scope: Numerical quadrature of alternative log-growth conditional on the stated reference central event; this is not a finite expected-stopping-time theorem. Dividing a log-threshold by these drifts is only an information-timescale heuristic.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Complete all-pairs U-statistics contain many dependent kernel evaluations; neither Hoeffding's bounded-U inequality nor standard first-order U-process symmetrization supports replacing n/2 by C(n,2) in a DKW-style confidence width.

The variance-CI e-process is intentionally Gaussian-parametric. It is not a distribution-free replacement for the pair-difference conditional CTM and should not be exported to heavy-tailed/non-Gaussian streams without a new reference-confidence and p-value argument.

The two variance channels consume one e-observation per two raw samples because disjoint future pairs are used to preserve conditional independence. Overlapping differences require a separate conditional e-process proof.
The r81d log-growth values are alternative expectations, not guarantees on realized or expected hitting time; overshoot and negative increments matter.

Global false-alarm <=0.05 is obtained by explicit union budgeting of two reference-good events and three conditional tests; no independence between the reference events or detector channels is assumed.

candidate_new.mechanism: Use identity-score conditional CTM for standardized mean-displacement information and exact Gaussian variance-confidence-superuniform p-values converted to e-processes for variance increase/decrease. This removes the pair-U-CDF calibration bottleneck, uses all 684 baseline observations for scale uncertainty, requires no learned score map, and covers the full unknown-mean/unknown-variance Gaussian KL>=1 alternative via the r80 branch argument.
candidate_new.status: theorem-level type-I structure and branch coverage; practical delay comparison still pending

frontier: Derive a formal alternative stopping-time bound for the variance-CI p-to-e channels, preferably via a fixed or mixture calibrator whose log-growth can be lower-bounded uniformly over r>=3.4 and r<=0.065 on the reference-good event; do not substitute the drift heuristic for a theorem.

Run common-random matched simulations under the exact global 0.05 budget for: early t/F sentinel, r81 raw-rank+variance-CI portfolio, r80 standardized x/x^2 conditional CTM, and the disjoint pair-difference CTM across the Gaussian KL=1 boundary.
Check whether using a predictable mixture over kappa improves variance-channel robustness without losing test-martingale validity; keep calibration choice fixed/predictable from past only.

Search for a special-kernel finite-sample U-CDF inequality for Gaussian pairwise differences only if it can beat the full-reference chi-square route; generic U-process bounds no longer justify spending frontier budget there.
Generalize the confidence-set-to-superuniform-p-to-e pattern to non-Gaussian scale families or robust scale confidence sequences, keeping the Gaussian result's exact scope separate.
exact_next_action: Prove a finite expected/high-probability stopping bound for the variance-CI p-to-e channel uniformly over the r>=3.4 and r<=0.065 branches, using the worst reference-CI endpoint and a fixed/mixture kappa. Then compare that formal bound and common-random empirical delay against the raw conditional-CTM branch and existing t/F sentinel under the same 0.05 global budget.
